## Adversarial Claim Verifier (voter 3/3)

Be SKEPTICAL. Try to REFUTE this claim. ≥2/3 refutations kill it.

## Research question
State of the art (as of July 2026) in AI coding-agent governance and harness design — the problem space of the claude.md-workflow repo: project instruction files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md-style), lifecycle hooks, deterministic verification gates, persistent agent memory/working-state across sessions and compaction, behavioral guardrails against scope creep/overclaiming/sycophancy, git-level enforcement, task contracts, and parallel multi-agent orchestration (worktree isolation, orchestrator/reduce patterns, adversarial review). Survey and compare best practices from: Anthropic (Claude Code, Agent SDK, skills/hooks/subagents), OpenAI (Codex, AGENTS.md), Google (Gemini CLI/Jules/Antigravity), Microsoft (GitHub Copilot agents, AutoGen/agent frameworks), NVIDIA (agent toolkits/NeMo), xAI (Grok agents/coding); and non-Western labs: Moonshot AI (Kimi K2.5 agentic training), Zhipu/Z.ai (GLM-5.x coding agents), DeepSeek (agentic/tool-use practices), Tencent (recent Hunyuan model launch and agent tooling), MiniMax (M-series agentic models), Alibaba Qwen if relevant; plus respected independents: Nous Research (Hermes 4/Hermes agent), Fundamental Research Labs (Peter Wang co-founder), the team behind the Ornith-1.0 LLM, tinygrad/George Hotz's approach to minimal harnesses, and any other influential open agent-harness projects (e.g. OpenHands, SWE-agent, Aider, Cline, Devin/Cognition). For each: what they prescribe for instruction-file structure and length, memory persistence, verification/eval gating, multi-agent patterns, and prompt-vs-deterministic enforcement. Identify convergent consensus, notable divergences (especially Western vs Chinese lab practices), and concrete, citable insights that should shape a 2026 rewrite of a drop-in governance kit for coding agents. Note if any named entity cannot be verified to exist (e.g. 'Ornith-1.0') rather than guessing.

## Claim under review
"GLM-5's agentic capability is trained via a new asynchronous reinforcement learning infrastructure that decouples generation from training, plus novel asynchronous agent RL algorithms for long-horizon interactions — indicating Zhipu invests in model-side RL training for agency rather than harness-side scaffolding."

**Source:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15763 (primary)
**Supporting quote:** "we implement a new asynchronous reinforcement learning infrastructure that drastically improves post-training efficiency by decoupling generation from training. Furthermore, we propose novel asynchronous agent RL algorithms that further improve RL quality, enabling the model to learn from complex, long-horizon interactions more effectively."

## Checklist
1. Is the claim actually supported by the quote, or is it an overreach/misread?
2. WebSearch for contradicting evidence — does any credible source dispute or heavily qualify this?
3. Is the source quality sufficient for the claim's strength? (extraordinary claims need primary sources)
4. Is the claim outdated? (check dates — old claims about fast-moving fields are suspect)
5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?

**refuted=true** if: unsupported by quote / contradicted / low-quality source for strong claim / outdated / marketing fluff.
**refuted=false** ONLY if: claim is well-supported, current, and source quality matches claim strength.
Default to refuted=true if uncertain.

Structured output only. Evidence MUST be specific.

# GLM-5 Paper Summary

**Title:** "GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering"

**Authors/Organization:** GLM-5-Team from Tsinghua University and affiliates (185+ authors listed, led by Aohan Zeng)

**Submission Date:** February 17, 2026 (revised February 24, 2026)

**Abstract Overview:**
The paper presents GLM-5, a foundation model advancing "the paradigm of vibe coding to agentic engineering." Key innovations include:

- **DSA implementation** to reduce computational costs while preserving long-context capabilities
- **Asynchronous RL infrastructure:** The authors describe a new approach that "drastically improves post-training efficiency by decoupling generation from training"
- **Asynchronous agent RL algorithms:** Novel methods enabling the model to "learn from complex, long-horizon interactions more effectively"

The model achieves top performance on open benchmarks and demonstrates strong real-world software engineering capabilities. Resources are available on GitHub at the provided repository link.

Web search results for query: "GLM-5 technical report asynchronous reinforcement learning arxiv Zhipu"

Links: [{"title":"GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering - ar5iv - arXiv","url":"https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2602.15763"},{"title":"GLM-5: Zhipu AI's Agentic Engineering Breakthrough","url":"https://llm-stats.com/blog/research/glm-5-launch"},{"title":"A Review of GLM-5: 744B-Parameter LLM Built for 200K Context and Agentic Training","url":"https://thesalt.substack.com/p/a-review-of-glm-5-744b-parameter"},{"title":"GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2602.15763v1"},{"title":"(PDF) GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering","url":"https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400895075_GLM-5_from_Vibe_Coding_to_Agentic_Engineering"},{"title":"Freshness-Aware Prioritized Experience Replay for LLM/VLM Reinforcement Learning","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16918"},{"title":"How to Use GLM-5.2: Complete Guide to Zhipu AI's 1M-Context Open-Source Coding Model | Tosea.ai","url":"https://tosea.ai/blog/glm-5-2-complete-guide"},{"title":"Paper page - GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering","url":"https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.15763"},{"title":"[2602.15763] GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15763"},{"title":"GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering GLM-5 Team","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.15763"}]

I found the GLM-5 technical report with information about asynchronous reinforcement learning from Zhipu AI and Tsinghua University on arXiv. Here's what I found:

## Overview

GLM-5 is a next-generation foundation model designed by Zhipu AI and Tsinghua University to transition from "vibe coding" to agentic engineering.

## Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning

The model implements a new asynchronous reinforcement learning infrastructure that drastically improves post-training efficiency by decoupling generation from training. The authors propose novel asynchronous agent RL algorithms that further improve RL quality, enabling the model to learn from complex, long-horizon interactions more effectively.

Building on the "slime" framework and the decoupled rollout engines initialized in GLM-4.5, the new infrastructure further decouples generation from training to maximize GPU utilization.

## Technical Specifications

The model scales to 744B parameters with a training token budget of 28.5T tokens.

The technical report is available on arXiv at: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15763

input.evidence: Verified against the primary source: arXiv:2602.15763 "GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering" (GLM-5 Team, Zhipu AI/Tsinghua, submitted 2026-02-17, revised 2026-02-24) exists and its abstract contains the quoted text verbatim: "a new asynchronous reinforcement learning infrastructure that drastically improves post-training efficiency by decoupling generation from training" and "novel asynchronous agent RL algorithms... enabling the model to learn from complex, long-horizon interactions more effectively." The claim's factual core is directly supported by the lab's own technical report (appropriate primary source for a claim about their training methodology, not a benchmark-superiority claim). Date is current (Feb 2026, ~5 months old). Two qualifications that do not rise to refutation: (1) the paper notes the infrastructure builds on the "slime" framework and decoupled rollout engines from GLM-4.5, so "new" is partly incremental rather than from-scratch; (2) the tail clause "rather than harness-side scaffolding" is the claimant's inference, not a paper statement — though it is consistent with Zhipu's observable strategy of optimizing GLM coding models for third-party harnesses (Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code) instead of a flagship proprietary harness. Recommend the survey phrase the contrast as "emphasis on model-side RL" rather than an exclusive either/or.
